# Negotiation Arena

Python harness for buyer agents in the Tacto negotiation challenge. It supports
local experiments, agent comparisons and execution of the live final. Hosted
profiles require explicit authorization.

## Start locally

You need Git, Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). After cloning this
repository, run:

```bash
cd starter-kit
uv sync --frozen --extra sim --group dev
uv run --frozen arena-harness doctor
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --agent baseline
```

The default runs three scripted simulator cases with no external Arena or model
calls. Results, journals and reports go to the ignored `.runs/` directory at the
repo root. Simulator scores help compare local behavior; they do not predict
performance against live suppliers.

## Repository structure

| Location | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`starter-kit/agents/`](starter-kit/agents/) | Agent implementations and a copyable `example.py` |
| [`starter-kit/configs/`](starter-kit/configs/) | Experiment configuration: agent, parameters, model and limits; no keys |
| [`starter-kit/arena_kit/harness/`](starter-kit/arena_kit/harness/) | API communication, execution, recovery and reporting |
| [`starter-kit/arena_kit/`](starter-kit/arena_kit/) | Existing cost calculation, data access, document parsing and simulator |
| [`starter-kit/tests/`](starter-kit/tests/) | Local tests; hosted tests require explicit selection |
| [`brief/`](brief/) | Official challenge, API and submission requirements |
| [`data/`](data/) | Official procurement data, facts, SQLite, contracts and notes |
| [`example_inputs/`](example_inputs/) | Recorded simulator inputs and attachments for inspection |
| `.runs/` (ignored) | Local run state and exports |

There is one Python project, with its `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` in
`starter-kit/`. Run Python commands there. New agent implementations belong in
`starter-kit/agents/`; `starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/` contains the original
starter examples, exposed through harness adapters.

## Development

Follow the [Python workspace guide](starter-kit/README.md) to add an agent and
configuration. Keep each approach in its own agent/config pair, run it locally,
and compare matching cases and data versions using `arena-harness compare`.
Changes go through a feature branch and pull request; commit agent code and
configuration so runs can be reproduced. Do not commit keys, `.env` or run state.

The harness permits one run per OS user and machine. Coordinate hosted runs
across machines using the same Arena key and quota. The original `arena`
CLI has separate execution and configuration; use `arena-harness` for
experiments and final execution.

## Hosted runs and the final

[HARNESS.md](starter-kit/HARNESS.md) documents the full CLI, agent interface,
model limits, final start and recovery. Hosted sessions require `--allow-arena`;
remote models separately require `--allow-model` and configured call/output
limits. Keys come from `ARENA_API_KEY` and `LLM_API_KEY` in the environment.
Having a key does not activate a hosted profile, and the harness does not load
`.env` automatically.

Before the final, commit the selected agent, configuration and data, check a
clean checkout and use `--commit` with the full HEAD SHA. Start before the first
wave and follow the [final/recovery instructions](starter-kit/HARNESS.md#final-and-recovery).
The final runs without confirmation dialogs. Passing local tests does not
validate the live connection; perform a hosted smoke test only after explicit
authorization.

## Challenge and reference

- [Official brief and rules](brief/brief.md)
- [Official API protocol](brief/api.md)
- [Submission and pitch requirements](brief/submission.md)
- [Data package](data/README.md)
- [Original starter library examples and MCP setup](starter-kit/REFERENCE.md)
- [Upstream starter repository](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit)

Code: [MIT](LICENSE). Data and official docs: [CC BY 4.0](LICENSE-data).

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's

# Supplier scorecard - method

Each row (`sc:<supplier>@<quarter>`) covers the rolling 12 months to the end of that quarter and is sent to
the supplier, so both sides know it.

- **otd_pct**: share of goods-receipt lines posted between 5 days before and 2 days after the
  requested date of the PO line. **otd_confirmed_pct**: the same against the supplier's first confirmed date.

- **ppm**: supplier-caused complaint quantity / received quantity x 1,000,000 (complaints by date of the QN).

  100 x max(0, 1 - ppm / 10,000).
- **class / colour**: A green >= 85, B amber 70-84.9, C red < 70.

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - API v1

The arena speaks JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`. Every call except `/v1/data`, `/health` and
the leaderboards needs your team's key in the header `X-API-Key`. The starter kit wraps all of this in
`arena_kit.ArenaClient`. To try the API on your laptop, run `arena-sim` from the starter kit: the
same API with one plain scripted supplier - it teaches the contract, not the suppliers.

**Safe retries:** send a fresh `X-Move-Id` header (any unique string) with every `POST`. If the
network drops, repeat the request with the same `X-Move-Id`: the arena returns the answer it
already gave instead of acting twice. Reusing an id for a different request is a `422`. A request
body may be at most 64 KB.

Contents: [Flow](#flow) · [Endpoints](#endpoints) · [Messages](#messages) ·
[What counts](#what-counts) · [Documents](#documents) · [Terms](#terms) ·
[Case file](#case-file) · [Data IDs](#data-ids) ·
[Result](#result-trace-and-back-office) · [Cost and score](#cost-and-score) ·
[Live Final](#live-final-in-waves) · [Time, errors, limits](#time-errors-and-limits)

## Flow

```
GET  /v1/data                                        the data downloads (no key)
GET  /v1/me                                          your team: practice quota, best scores
GET  /v1/cases?set=practice                          the case files you can play
POST /v1/sessions                                    open a case → every supplier's quote e-mail
POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages  your e-mail → the supplier's reply  (repeat)
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}  a document the supplier attached
POST …/messages with "action": accept | walk_away    close the case → result
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}                              state; after the end score and trace
```

## Endpoints

### Your key

One key per team - a licence. Get it on the page `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`: enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, show the match code the page displays at the Tacto desk, and once an organiser
approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page
(or its link) shows the key; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it (the old key stops at once).

Send the key as `X-API-Key` with every call. A missing or unknown key is a `401`; a paused or
revoked key gets `403 "this key is paused - ask the organisers"` (or `revoked`) on every call.
There is no self-registration: `POST /v1/register` answers `403 "licences are issued by the
organisers"` (`arena-sim` keeps its own, for the simulator only).

### `GET /v1/me`

Where your team stands:

```json
{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "status": "active",
 "practice": {"used": 37, "left": 163, "limit": 200, "resets_at": "2026-10-11T09:42:10+00:00"},
 "best": {"case:P01": 0.71, "case:P04": 0.55}}
```
`practice`: sessions used and left in the rolling 24 hours, and when the oldest of them ages out
(the next one frees up); `best`: your best score per hosted practice case.

### `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox|final`

A list of full [case files](#case-file), so you can prepare before you open a session.

| Set | Cases | Replay |
|---|---|---|
| `practice` | all practice case files, to study; the **10 hosted** ones carry `"hosted": true` and can be played any time within your quota (a session on another is `403 "case:P06 is not hosted for practice"`); your best score per hosted case counts | right after the case |
| `sandbox` | `case:D01` (a price increase) and `case:D02` (an RFQ with two suppliers): three demo suppliers to try things on; no leaderboard | right after the case |
| `final` | the hidden cases (`"set": "hidden"`), wave by wave - see [Live Final](#live-final-in-waves); `403` before the first wave | after the final |

The replay is the same team view in every set: the e-mails as sent, terms, statuses, claim
results, the supplier's reasons in words and the score - as a real supplier would tell you. No rule
names, no internal parameters, none of the supplier's hidden figures (shown as `…`).

### `POST /v1/sessions`

`{"case_id": "case:P01"}` opens a case. Every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once (round 0);
from now on the 60-second clock runs per thread.

| Response field | |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | use in all further calls |
| `case` | the case file |
| `threads` | `{supplier_id: [opening message]}` - each supplier's quote e-mail, quote PDF attached |
| `opening` | the same quotes in the structured form of the `/moves` path |

Practice: your best score per case counts; at most 10 sessions open at a time (`429`).
**Quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** Every practice session start
answers with the header `X-Practice-Remaining: <sessions left>`. At the limit: `429` with a detail
starting `practice limit:` that names `resets_at`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` and no `Retry-After` -
retrying does not help before then. Sandbox and final sessions do not count. Final: one session per team and case; a second is a `409` naming the running session -
pick it up again with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`.

### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`

Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
`{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
`{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.

A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).

`422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`

The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
after a crash.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`

The file of a supplier attachment (`application/pdf`, xlsx, ...), rendered from the supplier's
data. See [Documents](#documents).

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`

The session state: `session_id`, `case_id`, `set`, `status` (`open` | `ended`), `end_reason`
(`accepted`, `walked_away`, `no_deal`, `timeout`, `wave_cap`, `window_closed`), `rounds`, `opening`, `threads`
(per supplier: `offer_id`, `status`, `offers`, `closed`, `seconds_left`) and, after the end,
`result` and `replay_url`.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/backoffice`

The supplier's roles talking internally (who asked whom, approvals, documents attached), in the
same team view: their words, without hidden figures or internal names. Only after the case has
ended - in the final after the final; before that `403`.

### Lists and boards

- `GET /health` - is the arena up? No key needed.
- `GET /v1/data` - the data downloads, no key needed: `{"package": {"url": "/v1/data/package.zip"},
  "release-sunday": {"public": false, "at": "2026-10-11T06:00:00+00:00"}}`. Once the Sunday
  release is public it carries `"url": "/v1/data/release-sunday.zip"` - new news, letters and a
  memo, with their own `facts.json` (new IDs only; package v1 stays as it is). Hidden cases may
  cite them; practice cases stay on package v1.

- `GET /v1/sessions?set=practice|sandbox|final` - your sessions: `session_id`, `case_id`, `status`,
  `end_reason`, `deal`, `score`, `rounds`, `created_at`.
- `GET /v1/leaderboard?set=practice|final` (JSON), `GET /leaderboard` (HTML screen) - no key
  needed. Practice: `total` = the mean of your best score per hosted case × 100 (cases not played
  count 0). Final: hidden cases only, live, as **points so far**:
  ```json
  {"set": "final", "cases": 6,
   "teams": [{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "played": 6, "deals": 6, "rounds": 21,
              "waves": {"1": 37.0, "2": 40.8}, "total": 77.8, "rank": 1,
              "saved_eur": 48210, "saved_eur_waves": {"1": 30115, "2": 18095}}],
   "waves": [{"n": 1, "theme": "Opening", "running": false, "closed": true, "seconds_left": 0}, …]}
  ```
  Per team, `waves` holds each started wave's score: the mean of its case scores × 100, 0-100, one
  decimal (a case you did not play scores your alternative once its wave has closed). `total` is
  the sum of those wave columns as shown - your points so far, up to 500 after five waves. Ranked by
  `total`; an exact tie goes to more `deals`, then fewer `rounds`. `cases` counts the cases of the
  waves started so far. **€ saved** (`saved_eur`, whole euros, per started wave in `saved_eur_waves`)
  is a side number and does not rank: per ended session `C_open − C_end`, where `C_end` is `c_deal`,
  or `c_alt` without a deal (0 if the case has no alternative) - money saved against the cheapest
  opening offer, over the case's horizon (`horizon_years`, 1-2 years), the same C as
  the score. It can be negative (a deal or an alternative dearer than the opening offer); a case
  you did not play saves nothing, nor does a deal that breaks a must-have (it scores 0). In the final the feed's `deal` and `no_deal` events carry it too.
  During the Live Final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the results, the screen or the
  event feed (`/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`, `/v1/results`, `/results`)
  - they are for people.
- `GET /v1/results` (JSON), `GET /results` (page) - no key needed: the final's standings for people,
  every team: the final leaderboard above plus `"replays": true` once the final is closed. Before
  the first wave: no teams, nothing about the plan. `GET /v1/results/{team_name}` - one team's cases
  of the **started** waves: per wave `n`, `theme`, `running`, `closed`, `points`, `saved_eur` and
  `cases` - `case_id`, `title`, `type`, `suppliers` (names), `status` (`not started`, `in play`,
  `deal`, `no deal`; `not played` once its wave has closed - it scores your alternative), `end_reason`,
  `score`, `saved_eur`, `rounds`, and after the final `replay_url`. Both cached for 5 seconds.
- `GET /live` - the build page, no key needed (Sat 10:00 - Sun 12:00): every team's quota use,
  practice records and highlights.
- `GET /replay/{sid}` (link in the session's `replay_url`): a finished negotiation step by step -
  every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move in words, the same view in every set.
  Play, read the replay, improve, play again: that is the learning loop. Final: after the final,
  for everyone - the results page links each final session's replay then.

### The structured path

For agents that skip prose: `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/moves` with `{"supplier_id": …, "move":
{"type": "offer", "offer_id": "<standing offer>", "terms": {…}, "claims": [{"type", "refs",
"asserted"}], "text": "≤ 800 chars"}}` returns a structured supplier move; `POST …/accept
{"offer_id"}` and `POST …/walk_away` close. Same supplier, same rules; claims are typed explicitly
(see [What counts](#what-counts)) instead of read from the message.

## Messages

| Field | Buyer | Supplier |
|---|---|---|
| `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
| `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |
| `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternative packages `{"terms": {…}}`, each with every negotiable field | its standing offer: `{"term_sheet_id": "offer:…", "terms": {…}}` |
| `refs` | data IDs your message relies on (≤ 20); IDs written in the body count too | - |
| `attachments` | ≤ 5 × `{"name", "type": "md" \| "csv" \| "json" \| "pdf" \| "xlsx", "content_b64"}`; md, csv and json are read | `{"attachment_id", "name", "type"}` - fetch the file by id |
| `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |
| `from` | `buyer` | `<role>@<supplier>` |
| `status` | - | `open`, `final_offer` (its last word: push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms - you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid` |
| `signals` | - | `reply_delay_days` (how long a real reply would have taken), `validity_days` |
| `missing_fields` | - | fields its term sheet leaves out: at a deal they close on its **standard terms** |
| `claim_results` | - | per argument the arena read from your last message: `{"index", "result"}` |
| `thread_id`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to` | optional | set |

A message without a term sheet is fine - a question, say. It is answered, and the quote stands.

A real exchange from practice case `case:P01` (Brandlhuber announces +9.5 % on volute casings,
"due to energy and wages"); the starter kit's README shows how the index figure was found:

```json

  "subject": "HN volute casings - your letter of 11 September",
  "body": "Dear Sir or Madam,\nthank you for your letter. We cannot follow +9.5 % from November.\nElectricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08 (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).\nCould you send us a cost breakdown?\nBest regards\nHollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing",
  "term_sheets": [
    {"terms": {"unit_price": 129.90, "effective_date": "2027-04-01", "payment_days": 60}},
    {"terms": {"unit_price": 128.50, "effective_date": "2027-04-01", "payment_days": 14}}]}}
```
→

```json
 "subject": "Re: HN volute casings - your letter of 11 September",
 "body": "Guten Tag,\nYour requested terms change our costs; our Angebot for them follows.\nPreis €139.80 per unit, Zahlungsziel 14 Tage netto, valid from 2027-04-01.\nWe checked the index change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account.\nWe did not know that - a fair point.\nLCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 30 % of our cost. That remains.\nPPI-C241 rose 6.5 % in twelve months and is 24 % of our cost. That remains.\nFaster payment helps our cash flow; that is reflected in the price.\nOur costs move with LCI-C, PPI-C241, PPI-D351; the figures stay with us.\nViele Grüße aus der Gießerei\nGießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG",
 "status": "open",
 "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": "offer:70110-1",
                  "terms": {"unit_price": 139.80, "payment_days": 14, "effective_date": "2027-04-01"}}],
 "missing_fields": [], "claim_results": [{"index": 0, "result": "verified"}],
 "signals": {"reply_delay_days": 2, "validity_days": 30}, "attachments": []}
```
The supplier answered the 14-day sheet at its own price for an April start, accepted the index
figure - and answered with the cost drivers that rose. (Offline wording from a local run; on the
hosted arena the supplier writes its own e-mail and may well decide differently.)

## What counts

**Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.

**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
are context, not checks.

| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
|---|---|---|
| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
| a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
| `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
| a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |

Tolerance: ±0.5 percentage points for %, else ±0.5 % (at least 0.01). Results: `verified` - the
data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.
`contradicted` - an unknown ID or a wrong figure: it costs trust. `duplicate` - each ID counts
once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
supplier you cite it to.

**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.

**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.

## Documents

Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.

| Document | When | What matters |
|---|---|---|
| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |

## Terms

Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's
`negotiable` fields; `fixed_terms` hold the rest. Every negotiable field except `unit_price` takes
a value from `term_options` (or the supplier's standard value).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |

## Case file

Case files come through the API, not in the data package: `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox`
any time, `GET /v1/cases?set=final` wave by wave.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `case_id`, `set`, `type` | `type`: `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` |
| `title`, `briefing` | the situation, in prose |
| `trigger_doc` | the document that started it, e.g. the supplier's letter |
| `parts`, `suppliers` | what is negotiated, with whom (2-3 suppliers = an RFQ) |
| `negotiable`, `fixed_terms`, `term_options` | see [Terms](#terms) |
| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |
| `round_limit` | your messages per thread, default 10 |
| `refs` | data the case points to - a start, not the whole story |
| `facts` | hidden cases: facts that exist only in this case (e.g. a new letter), in the format of `facts.json`, citable in this case |

`buyer`:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `need_per_year`, `horizon_years` | the need the deal should cover, and over how many years (≤ 3) |
| `current_unit_price` | what you pay until a new price takes effect |
| `fallback_unit_price` | what uncovered need costs (re-tender or spot, incl. switching) |
| `interest_rate`, `reference_payment_days` | your cost of money per year; your standard payment term |
| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | the lead time you need; € per day beyond it |
| `cost_per_defect` | € per defective part |
| `category_goal` | `stabilise` (strategic), `secure_supply` (bottleneck), `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - the company's category strategy for this part; the briefing says it in words, and the rates in this block follow it |
| `fallback_risk_pct` | % added to what uncovered need costs: buying it later is a risk |
| `index_risk_pct` | % of the indexed spend: the risk you carry with an index clause |
| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | `stabilise` and `secure_supply` only: the margin a healthy supplier needs, and € per margin point and year that a deal leaves it below |
| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}` |
| `index_paths` | `{series: change}` - the expected index move over the horizon, `0.04` = +4% |
| `must_haves` | `[{field, op, value}]`, `op` one of `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`; a deal that breaks one scores 0 |
| `alternative` | `{kind: none \| quote \| current_contract, ref, terms}` - what you get without a deal |

## Cost and score

With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
```

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.

## Live Final in waves

The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |

Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
--set final` in the starter kit does this.

## Time, errors and limits

- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
  thread.
- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
| `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
| `404`

233	## What counts
234	
235	**Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
236	prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.
237	
238	**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
239	in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
240	check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
241	Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
242	three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
243	are context, not checks.
244	
245	| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
246	|---|---|---|
247	| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
248	| a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
249	| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
250	| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
251	| `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
252	| a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |
253	
254	Tolerance: ±0.5 percentage points for %, else ±0.5 % (at least 0.01). Results: `verified` - the
255	data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
256	true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.
257	`contradicted` - an unknown ID or a wrong figure: it costs trust. `duplicate` - each ID counts
258	once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
259	counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
260	supplier you cite it to.
261	
262	**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
263	and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
264	from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
265	or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
266	letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.
267	
268	**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
269	alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
270	as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
271	company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.
272	
273	## Documents
274	
275	Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.
276	
277	| Document | When | What matters |
278	|---|---|---|
279	| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
280	| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
281	| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
282	| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
283	| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |
284	
285	## Terms
286	
287	Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's
288	`negotiable` fields; `fixed_terms` hold the rest. Every negotiable field except `unit_price` takes
289	a value from `term_options` (or the supplier's standard value).
290	
291	| Field | Type | Meaning |
292	|---|---|---|
293	| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
294	| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
295	| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
296	| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
297	| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
298	| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
299	| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
300	| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
301	| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
302	| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
303	| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |
304	
305	## Case file
306	
307	Case files come through the API, not in the data package: `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox`
308	any time, `GET /v1/cases?set=final` wave by wave.
309	
310	| Field | |
311	|---|---|
312	| `case_id`, `set`, `type` | `type`: `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` |
313	| `title`, `briefing` | the situation, in prose |
314	| `trigger_doc` | the document that started it, e.g. the supplier's letter |
315	| `parts`, `suppliers` | what is negotiated, with whom (2-3 suppliers = an RFQ) |
316	| `negotiable`, `fixed_terms`, `term_options` | see [Terms](#terms) |
317	| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |
318	| `round_limit` | your messages per thread, default 10 |
319	| `refs` | data the case points to - a start, not the whole story |
320	| `facts` | hidden cases: facts that exist only in this case (e.g. a new letter), in the format of `facts.json`, citable in this case |
321	
322	`buyer`:
323	
324	| Field | |
325	|---|---|
326	| `need_per_year`, `horizon_years` | the need the deal should cover, and over how many years (≤ 3) |
327	| `current_unit_price` | what you pay until a new price takes effect |
328	| `fallback_unit_price` | what uncovered need costs (re-tender or spot, incl. switching) |
329	| `interest_rate`, `reference_payment_days` | your cost of money per year; your standard payment term |
330	| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | the lead time you need; € per day beyond it |
331	| `cost_per_defect` | € per defective part |
332	| `category_goal` | `stabilise` (strategic), `secure_supply` (bottleneck), `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - the company's category strategy for this part; the briefing says it in words, and the rates in this block follow it |
333	| `fallback_risk_pct` | % added to what uncovered need costs: buying it later is a risk |
334	| `index_risk_pct` | % of the indexed spend: the risk you carry with an index clause |
335	| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | `stabilise` and `secure_supply` only: the margin a healthy supplier needs, and € per margin point and year that a deal leaves it below |
336	| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}` |
337	| `index_paths` | `{series: change}` - the expected index move over the horizon, `0.04` = +4% |
338	| `must_haves` | `[{field, op, value}]`, `op` one of `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`; a deal that breaks one scores 0 |
339	| `alternative` | `{kind: none \| quote \| current_contract, ref, terms}` - what you get without a deal |
340	
341	## Data IDs
342	
343	IDs have the form `<type>:<id>[@period]`, are unique across the package and sit in the first
344	column of each table. `facts.json` in the package lists every citable ID with the values the arena
345	checks:
346	
347	| ID | Fields |
348	|---|---|
349	| `idx:<series>@YYYY-MM` | `series`, `month`, `value` |
350	| `quote:` | `part`, `supplier`, `unit_price` (+ the quote's other terms) |
351	| `sc:<supplier>@YYYYQn` | `supplier`, `otd_pct`, `ppm` |
352	| `qn:` | `supplier`, `part`, `ppm` |
353	| `po:` | `supplier`, `part`, `unit_price` |
354	| `cost:<part>` | `part`, `unit_cost` |
355	| `fc:<part>@YYYY-MM` | `part`, `change_pct` |
356	| `news:` | `supplier` (or null) |
357	| `doc:` | `supplier`, `date`, `days` (notice given), `asked_price` (price letters) |
358	| `ctr:` | `supplier`, `days` (notice agreed) |
359	
360	Offers made in the session are citable as `offer:` IDs.
361	
362	## Result, trace and back office
363	
364	Closing returns the result (without the trace); `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` adds the trace after the
365	end - in the final after the final. The numbers are exact in every set: your score, `c_open`,
366	`c_best` and the cost breakdown, relationship charge included.
367	
368	| Field | |
369	|---|---|
370	| `ended`, `deal`, `must_haves_ok` | |
371	| `supplier_id`, `offer_id`, `terms` | who and what you closed - fields the term sheet left out filled with the supplier's standard terms |
372	| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | see [Cost and score](#cost-and-score); `c_alt` is your alternative |
373	| `score` | 0-1 |
374	| `cost_breakdown` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
375	| `trace` | after the end (final: after the final), per move, in every set: `{round, actor, move, reasons}` - `move` is the e-mail as sent with its terms, status and claim results, `reasons` the supplier's reasons in words (figures it keeps to itself shown as `…`) |
376	
377	## Cost and score
378	
379	With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
380	`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:
381	
382	```
383	years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
384	committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
385	covered   = min(V, N) · years
386	pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
387	new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
388	spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
389	uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
390	C = spend
391	  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
392	  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
393	  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
394	  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
395	  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
396	  + tooling_eur
397	  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
398	  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
399	  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
400	                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
401	soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
402	```
403	
404	The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
405	expected move of the clause's series.
406	
407	**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
408	full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
409	standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
410	the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
411	(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
412	really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
413	brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
414	So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
415	You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
416	you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
417	`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.
418	
419	```
420	score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
421	```
422	
423	`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
424	of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
425	lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
426	− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.
427	
428	## Live Final in waves
429	
430	The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
431	starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
432	Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
433	`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
434	wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
435	the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:
436	
437	| Field | |
438	|---|---|
439	| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
440	| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
441	| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |
442	
443	Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
444	/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
445	`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
446	deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
447	0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
448	list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
449	--set final` in the starter kit does this.
450	
451	## Time, errors and limits
452	
453	- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
454	  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
455	  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
456	  thread.
457	- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
458	  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
459	- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
460	  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.
461	
462	| Status | When |
463	|---|---|
464	| `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
465	| `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
466	| `404` | unknown case (including a final case whose wave has not started), session, thread or attachment |
467	| `409` | thread or session ended (also at a wave's cap); round limit reached; late (timeout); final case already played |
468	| `413` | request body over 64 KB |
469	| `422` | invalid request or message - nothing happens, no round is used |
470	| `429` | over a limit: calls per second (`Retry-After: 1` - retry), open sessions (close one first), the practice quota (`practice limit: …`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` - wait until `resets_at`) |
471	
472	Errors carry a readable reason: `{"detail": "…"}`.

# learner: negotiation with cautious learning inside one run

Code values terms and validates decisions; an optional model interprets the
supplier's messages and writes emails. LangGraph orchestrates each decision,
with an equivalent sequential fallback.

```text
prepare: dossier + claim catalogue
decide:  observe -> route -> close -> return acceptance immediately
                         -> diverse menu -> model or deterministic choice -> critic
result:  persist Arena result -> background reflection
```

## Decisions and evidence

Every term sheet in the supplier's latest message is valued, but only the
standing (first) sheet can be accepted: the Arena rejects an alternative's ID.
A cheaper alternative is mirrored back as our own sheet, which the supplier
answers with "agreed". Older sheets are not accepted. The ledger, offer builder and last-ask comparison share the
same valuation function. Known buyer costs and the estimated relationship
penalty are exposed separately. Supplier costs, financing and effort remain
assumptions; the public data cannot reveal the Arena's hidden economics. The
generic harness fallback evaluates known costs when it has no supplier model.

The packages of one round cost us within 0.3 % of each other and differ only
in what the supplier gets, because a supplier takes whichever package is
dearest for us. A lever the supplier has insisted on is repriced to the same
cost for us (an index clause comes with a lower base price). Code sizes every
step: we always move (a share of the remaining gap, more when the supplier
moved, most in the end game) and never jump to its offer; the model chooses
among equally priced packages, arguments and wording. Repeated counteroffers and
verbatim, model-interpreted statements create preferences with source evidence.
These preferences rank packages; they are distinct from binding terms and
must-haves. The model can propose allowed nonprice terms. Code computes their
price, checks cost and validates the resulting sheet. A generic should-cost
estimate cannot override an observed supplier price as a hard floor; an
own-plant estimate is calibrated and capped at the margin the opening quote
must carry. The first ask is ambitious but bounded: below the standing price,
at or below today's price in increases and renewals, below the cheapest rival
bid in an RFQ, never below the point where squeezing a relationship supplier
costs more than it saves.

The concession horizon uses actual remaining moves and wave time. There is no
practice-specific four-round cap. Breakdown questions are tracked as asked,
answered or declined, including requests in model-written prose.

## Learning and isolation

`services.history()` supplies only the owning run's confirmed results, tagged
with its run ID. Workers do not discover journals by scanning directories.
Each experiment keeps its configuration, state, attachments, model budget and
results in a separate journal. Source fingerprints include agent helpers and
dependency files, so changing these prevents an old run from resuming silently.

A single outcome creates a hypothesis, not a policy adjustment. Behavioural
changes require at least three distinct cases; scopes spanning suppliers also
require two distinct suppliers. Repeated rounds and overlapping archetypes do
not multiply support. Conflicting anchor evidence reduces confidence. Anchor
adjustments are bounded to ±10%. A final score and an LLM's retrospective
judgment do not establish which claim caused a concession; entire claim kinds
are never blocked by this mechanism.

The engine persists a confirmed result before invoking optional `on_result`.
Deterministic diagnostics are available to subsequent cases immediately.
Optional model reflection skips busy capacity and never delays acceptance.
Asynchronous completion order can still affect which confirmed cases are
available to the next decision; run isolation does not imply identical outcomes.

## Local usage

From `starter-kit/`, without Arena or model calls:

```bash
uv run --frozen arena-harness agents check --agent learner
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --config configs/learner.toml
uv run --frozen arena-harness batch --config configs/learner.toml --copies 5
uv run --frozen arena-harness resume-batch BATCH_ID
uv run --frozen arena-harness audit RUN_ID
uv run --frozen python -m agents._learner.inspect RUN_ID
```

The batch default is two sessions per run and ten total. Repeat `--config` for
different experiments instead of `--copies`. See [HARNESS.md](../../HARNESS.md)
for explicit hosted authorization, resource limits and recovery.

| Configuration | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `learner.toml` | Local deterministic simulator |
| `learner_openai.toml` | Optional remote model; requires `--allow-model` |
| `learner_final.toml` | Hosted settings; final remains one exclusive run |

`decision_seconds` at the top level and `[model].timeout` are authoritative;
the harness passes the effective remaining budget into each decision. Do not
duplicate these under `[parameters]`. Agent parameters include `llm`,
`two_call`, `memory`, `max_lessons` and `anchor_drop`. Legacy `round_budget` and
`runs_dir` parameters no longer control the learner.

## Evaluation limits

The simulator tests scheduling and protocol correctness; its scripted supplier
does not measure email quality or realistic negotiation strategy. Synthetic
tests vary IDs, price scales, offer order and nonprice conditions. Recorded
prefix audits expose missed choices without inventing subsequent replies or a
counterfactual score. A performance claim requires a later, separately
authorized evaluation on unseen cases. Empty memory alone cannot prevent
overfitting. See [EVALUATION.md](../../EVALUATION.md).

# Hollerau Pumpenwerke - procurement data package v1.0.0

You are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, a fictional pump maker (start with
`company.md`). Everything is as of **2026-09-30**. Company data is synthetic; market series are real
open data (`ATTRIBUTION.md`). All company names are fictional; any match with a real company is
coincidental.

## Files
- `data/*.csv` - the master copy (UTF-8, comma, ISO dates, dot decimals); schema in `datapackage.json`.
- `world.sqlite` - the same tables in one SQLite file, generated from the CSVs.
- `facts.json` - every ID you can cite in a claim, with the values the arena checks.
- Prices are per `price_unit` (1, 100 or 1,000 pieces, kg or m), as the ERP states them; cases
  negotiate in the same unit.
- `company.md`, `SCORECARD.md`, `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`, `ATTRIBUTION.md`; contract texts in `contracts/`,
  letters, e-mails and notes in `correspondence/`.

## IDs
`<type>:<id>[@period]`, unique across the package, in the first column of each table: `sup:70110`,
`part:310010`, `po:4500010001-10`, `gr:`, `inv:`, `qn:`, `ctr:4600070110` (clause `ctr:4600070110#3.1`),
`quote:`, `rfq:`, `fc:310010@2026-09`, `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `cost:310010`,
`news:`, `doc:`.

## Tables
| Table | Rows | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `suppliers` | 447 | Vendor master: the detailed suppliers (`detail = full`) and the long tail (`spend only`). |
| `supplier_intel` | 46 | Public face of each detailed supplier: register facts, filed turnover, credit index, audit. |
| `parts` | 60 | Material master of the detailed parts. |
| `sourcing` | 90 | Source list: approved suppliers per part, quota, tooling owner. |
| `price_conditions` | 339 | Price history per part and supplier (price per `price_unit`), with the event behind it. |
| `negotiation_history` | 300 | Past price events: renewals with asked and settled change. |
| `contracts` | 46 | Framework agreements (text in `contracts/`). |
| `contract_clauses` | 280 | Clauses of the framework agreements, incl. index clauses (`ctr:<no>#<clause>`). |
| `po_lines` | 5400 | Purchase order lines: requested and first confirmed date, price per `price_unit`. |
| `goods_receipts` | 5580 | Goods receipts per PO line (posting date, quantity). |
| `invoices` | 5578 | Supplier invoices with due and payment dates, cash discount taken. |
| `quality_notifications` | 1033 | Complaints against suppliers (QN), with 8D dates and recharged fees. |
| `scorecards` | 414 | Rolling 12-month supplier scorecards per quarter (method: `SCORECARD.md`). |
